title: Halves, Fourths and Eighths
seo_title: Grade 2 Halves, Fourths and Eighths Worksheets (TEKS 2.3)
standard_text: 2.3A partition objects into equal parts and name the parts, including halves, fourths, and eighths, using words; 2.3B explain that the more fractional parts used to make a whole, the smaller the part; and the fewer the fractional parts, the larger the part; 2.3C use concrete models to count fractional parts beyond one whole using words and recognize how many parts it takes to equal one whole; 2.3D identify examples and non-examples of halves, fourths, and eighths
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 fraction worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.3: equal parts, halves, fourths and eighths, more parts make smaller parts and counting parts beyond one whole. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Halves, fourths and eighths are equal parts of a whole.
key_sub: More parts make smaller parts. 4 fourths make one whole.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A fraction part must be one of several equal parts.
  • 2 equal parts are halves, 4 are fourths, 8 are eighths.
  • The more parts a whole is cut into, the smaller each part.
  • 2 halves, 4 fourths or 8 eighths make one whole. Five fourths is one whole and one more fourth.

Examples

Example

A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. 3 are eaten.

8 equal parts are eighths

Answer: three eighths

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling unequal parts fourthsFourths must be 4 equal parts.
Thinking more parts make bigger partsEighths are smaller than fourths.
Not knowing what makes a whole4 fourths make 1 whole.

items.q: How many halves make 1 whole?
items.e: A whole cut into 2 equal shares has 2 halves. 2 halves make 1 whole.

items.q: Mia cuts a pizza into fourths. How many fourths make the whole pizza?
items.e: Fourths means 4 equal shares. The whole pizza is 4 fourths. (It is not 3: count the shares, not the cuts.)

items.q: 2 halves make a whole. How many fourths make a whole?
items.e: Fourths are 4 equal shares, so 4 fourths make a whole. 2 fourths make only a half.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole circle?
items.e: The whole circle is four fourths. 1 is shaded, so 3 more must be shaded: 1 + 3 = 4.

items.q: How many more fourths must be shaded to shade the whole rectangle?
items.e: The whole rectangle is four fourths. 2 are shaded, so 2 more must be shaded: 2 + 2 = 4.

items.q: Which is smaller: half of a sandwich or a fourth of the same sandwich?
items.e: 4 is more than 2, so a fourth is smaller. More shares means smaller shares.

items.q: Shapes A and B are the same size. Which shaded share is bigger?
items.e: A is cut into halves. B is cut into fourths. A half is bigger than a fourth, so A is bigger. (4 is more than 2, but more shares means smaller shares.)
